requests.title: Approve compiled package v4.1 as the implementation plan for November 7
requests.question: Approve requirements-compiled/v4.1 (on top of package v4, whose verification plan it uses unchanged) as the plan the event build follows: interface contracts, file ownership, state-machine tables, GitHub error matrix, Forma layout contract, verification execution plan and schedule?
options: A: approve v4.1, after v4 is approved (ODR-V4-01)
C: decline; build from v4 alone
requests.recommendation: A. v4.1 changes no requirement, obligation or test binding (preservation-report.json); it removes decisions the team would otherwise make inside the timed window.
requests.rationale: Only the owner approves a package (RDP-003). v4.1 depends on v4: approving v4.1 without v4 leaves the requirements unfrozen.
requests.impact: Until approved, v4.1 is a CANDIDATE. The event build may follow it as guidance but must report it unapproved.

requests.title: Freeze the v4.1 interface contracts at T14, superseding FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES sections 42 and 46 for Causa
requests.question: docs/FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES.md section 42 (IInvestigationStore with ProviderConflict) and section 46 (LocalStore.fs) contradict ADR-R7-001 and PERSIST-003 (finding F41-01), and docs/rehearsal-007/traceability.json does not list them as superseded. Should the v4.1 contracts (IF41-STORAGE, IF41-SAVE) be the frozen Causa boundary in their place?
options: A: yes; record sections 42 and 46 as superseded for Causa
requests.recommendation: A. PERSIST-001 gives the persistence requirements precedence over older type shapes; the v4.1 contracts typecheck and implement the seven-state machine of SM-SAVE without a new state.
requests.rationale: An agent may not edit a superseded design document on its own; the contradiction must be decided.
requests.impact: With B, the interface freeze at T14 waits for the reconciliation, and the schedule gain from interface-first work is lost.

requests.title: Accept the interface-first ordering changes of the v4.1 DAG
requests.question: v4.1 lets the interface freeze (T14) start before the kernel (T13) and the invariant tests (T12), and the save machine (T19) and GitHub provider (T20) start before the kernel, because the frozen contracts fix the types. It keeps the invariant tests before the save machine (T12 before T19, R4-01) and the kernel before integration checkpoint 1 (T13 before T17) and before live integration (T13 before T21). The six v4 orderings it drops are listed with reasons in analysis/task-adjustments.json waivedPrecedences: T12 before T14, T13 before T14, T13 before T19, T13 before T20, T12 before T35, T13 before T35. Accept them?
requests.recommendation: A. With v4's estimates, the ordering changes alone shorten the critical path from 340 to 305 minutes and topology C from 405 to 395 (schedule.json scenarios). Neither alone nor with ODR-V41-04 does topology A fit the 420-minute window; C fits in every scenario.
requests.rationale: The change moves integration risk from T19 to T21 (optimization-report.md, risks R41-02 and R41-03); the owner decides whether that trade is acceptable.
requests.impact: With B, the agent removes the dependency changes from task-adjustments.json and recompiles; the other v4.1 artifacts still apply.

requests.title: Accept the v4.1 estimate changes
requests.question: v4.1 lowers five timed estimates (minutes): T12 25 to 15, T14 20 to 15, T16 35 to 30, T18 45 to 35, T22 70 to 60. It also gives preflight T10 an estimate of 25 outside the window. Each reason is in analysis/task-adjustments.json; all are the package author's estimates, not measurements. Accept them for planning?
requests.recommendation: A only if the reasons convince you: with v4's dependencies, the estimate changes alone take the critical path from 340 to 325 minutes and C from 405 to 390; with ODR-V41-03 also accepted, 285 and 380.
requests.rationale: Lower estimates move the schedule without moving the work; only the owner accepts them.
requests.impact: With B, the agent restores v4's estimates and recompiles; reserves are unchanged either way.

requests.title: Map UI-016's amber #E9A23B to a Forma token
requests.question: UI-016 (docs/CAUSA-UI-EXPERIENCE-REQUIREMENTS.md) names the identity colour amber #E9A23B and requires every colour to map to a named semantic Forma theme token. Forma 0.12.0 defines no such value (its ambers differ), and v4.1 forbids declaring new --ef-* properties. Which applies?
options: A: use Forma's warning-status token for amber, keeping text labels (DEC-R7-002)
B: allow web/causa.css to declare one theme token for #E9A23B, outside the --ef-* namespace, after measuring contrast
C: ask Forma for a release with the identity colours
requests.recommendation: A for November 7: it uses only published tokens; B or C if the exact hex is required.
requests.rationale: A requirement value and the no-invented-token rule conflict; an agent may not resolve that by itself.
requests.impact: Until decided, FL-06 cites #E9A23B as the requirement's value (check X07 accepts a literal only with its requirement source).
